To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the TPUv2 unit with 8 cores can process 40 000 images per second with the prediction loss equal 0.05 (for MNIST and FashionMNIT datasets) and (ii) the TPU can process 512 images per second with training loss equal 0,001 (for MNIST dataset).

(1) the TPUv2 cores can process the data in the batch size up to 512 images for training and up to 40 000 images (or 1 600 000 pixels) for prediction, and (2) TPUv2 is up to 10 times faster than the NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPU for training, and 2 times faster for prediction (with and without overheads), and (3) the prediction accuracy and training loss do not change significantly for

the performance of TPUv3 units is better for the training phase and performance of TPU2 is better for the inference phase, but the speedup of TPUv1 and TPUv2 over the GPU is significant only for large batch sizes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of the maximally allowed batch size (for better runtime) on the performance of graphic processing unit (GPU) and the tensor processing unit (TPU) in the training and inference phases of the selected deep learning model.
the influence of batch size (and the number of images per batch) on the performance of the GPU and TPU during training and prediction phases.
the practical aspects of using TPUv2 for the training and prediction of DNNs and can be used to optimize the usage of Google Cloud TPUs for DNN training and prediction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TPUv2 is more efficient for the prediction phase, and the GPU is more efficient for training phase.
TPUv2 is a better choice than GPU for training phase, while GPU is a better choice for prediction phase.
the TPUv2 is a promising solution for training and prediction of DNNs, especially for the datasets with large images and/or large batch sizes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TPUv2 usage can be beneficial for the DNN training and prediction tasks for the datasets with images of sizes >28x28.

for the low-scale usage of TPUv3 units (8 cores) it is possible to achieve the same prediction accuracy as for the quite powerful NVIDIA GPU card with the speedups up to 10 times for training stage (with and with taking into account overhead) and speedup 2x for inference stage (without taking in account overheads).
the TPUv2 is a promising alternative to the GPUs in terms of the prediction accuracy and the speedup for the datasets with images of sizes up to 28x28.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the utilization of TPUs is beneficial for training of deep learning models with the batch sizes larger than 512 images, and for prediction phase for batch sizes larger than about 40 000 images.

TPUv2 can provide a significant speedup for training and prediction phases of DNNs even for low-scale TPUv2 utilization, and the batch size should be chosen in such a way that the utilization of the TPUv2 unit is maximized.

TPUv2 is the best choice for the prediction phase (inference), and GPU is the best choice when the number of training samples is limited (for example, in the case of a small dataset or when the dataset is being collected during training).
